- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via DashboardWidgetSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1f8ce8658b937d3685df62b04e2e478430b8e83` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `45a8676ff86f5095d47cc092b6a09c04cc56d6a6` — the merge of head `e1494c7206fcd7d16d5446fbb98dce842e58dff3` into base `d1f8ce8658b937d3685df62b04e2e478430b8e83`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 45a8676ff86f5095d47cc092b6a09c04cc56d6a6 && git checkout 45a8676ff86f5095d47cc092b6a09c04cc56d6a6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d1f8ce8658b937d3685df62b04e2e478430b8e83 e1494c7206fcd7d16d5446fbb98dce842e58dff3 && git checkout -B drift-repro d1f8ce8658b937d3685df62b04e2e478430b8e83 && git merge --no-ff e1494c7206fcd7d16d5446fbb98dce842e58dff3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1f8ce8658b937d3685df62b04e2e478430b8e83
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d1f8ce8658b937d3685df62b04e2e478430b8e83` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e1494c7206fcd7d16d5446fbb98dce842e58dff3`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20958 (body, the claim comment and the os-dev-report), PR #21053 (body, the nine-file list, the net diff against `main`), the files at the head through `git show` (reading only), and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **Narrowing at `DashboardWidgetSchema.values`** — a widget whose `dimensions` is absent or an empty array, whose `values` carries two or more members, and whose `type` is `pie`, `donut`, `funnel`, `scatter`, `radar`, `treemap` or `sankey` is refused with ONE `custom` issue at `values`, naming the widget `id`, the count and the authored type. **Right.** This is the card's scope item 1 exactly, and every card pin is covered by a test: the seven refused (also with an explicit `dimensions: []`), the same seven accepted with one dimension or with one measure, and every member of the multi-measure set accepted dimensionless with three measures (the control).
2. **The metric family (`metric` / `kpi` / `gauge` / `solid-gauge` / `bullet`, and a typeless widget, which defaults to `metric`) is stepped over by the new check.** The card's prose says "outside the multi-measure set", which read literally would include the family; the card's pin "the metric family's existing refusal is unchanged" decides it. **Right:** firing on the family would turn one issue into two on the same `values`, and the diff pins the family's refusal byte-identical to the metric export's direct call. The taxonomy test pins seven plus five plus the eight-member set equal to `ChartTypeSchema.options`; I counted the enum at the head: twenty members, so the partition is exhaustive and a new chart type reddens that test rather than slipping past both checks.
3. **New public export `DASHBOARD_WIDGET_MULTI_MEASURE_TYPES`** (`table`, `pivot`, `bar`, `column`, `horizontal-bar`, `line`, `area`, `combo`, `as const satisfies readonly ChartType[]`). **Right:** the card's "one exported constant". All eight are declared `ChartTypeSchema` members, `ChartType` is exported from `chart.zod.ts` at the head, and `ui/index.ts` ships `dashboard.zod` wholesale, so the barrel carries it. The check, the refusal text and the `values` doc string all read it. At the head the only other literal of the set in the repo is the expectation in `dashboard.test.ts` that pins the constant's content, which is a test reading, not a second list any code consults. The card's "no second list" holds.
4. **New public export `checkDashboardWidgetDimensionlessMeasureArity`** (arity 2, chained by identifier after `checkDashboardWidgetMetricMeasureArity`). The card names only the constant as an export. **Right anyway:** the card's "Then" section requires objectui's mirror to re-attach the check as it did for the metric family, which needs the function exported; `object-refinement-check-exports.test.ts` pins one export per `custom` check on the schema; and the metric-family precedent commit `09e16a574` exported its check for the same reason. The changeset names both exports on its Clause-② line.
5. **Export behaviour off the spec's door.** The export returns on a `type` outside `ChartTypeSchema.options` and on a typeless widget (the default is a family member). **Right:** through the door the default is applied before object-level checks (`ChartTypeSchema.default('metric')` at the head) and an unknown type aborts on `invalid_value`, so the export refuses exactly what the door refuses when objectui chains it onto its wider, default-less enum. `dimensions` is `z.array(z.string()).optional()`, so a non-array `dimensions` is the field's own `invalid_type` through the door and the check's early return there is unreachable, which is harmless.
6. **The `values` doc string** gains "with no dimensions, two or more only on" followed by the constant joined with slashes; the two `DashboardWidget` rows of `content/docs/references/ui/dashboard.mdx` carry the same text. **Right:** a shipped doc string change consistent with the rule, regenerated rather than hand-edited.
7. **ADR-0087 semantic entry** `18.dashboard-widget-dimensionless-multi-measure-refused.ts`, plus the registry lap. **Right:** the registry hunk sits inside the os-generated semantic:18 region (the markers at the head wrap it), sorted by id between `dashboard-widget-chart-config-structure-refused` and `dashboard-widget-metric-family-multi-measure-refused`, and the entry's surface, replacement, reason and acceptance criteria describe the same rule the check implements (the seven, absent-or-empty `dimensions`, two or more `values`, one `custom` issue at `values`, the family stepped over, the type refusal alone on an unknown type).
8. **No `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment.** **Right:** the registry's own docblock reads "one fragment per retirement"; this entry is a semantic narrowing with no conversion, and the precedent commit `09e16a574` added none either (its registry diff is one hunk in the semantic region and touches no fragment line).
9. **`api-surface/ui.json` and `export-origins/ui.json`** gain exactly the two symbols above and remove nothing. **Right**, and consistent with the barrel.
10. **No consumer fixture moves.** The card's census and the dev's census both read zero authored dimensionless multi-measure widgets on the seven; the file list holds none. **Right.**
11. **File surface.** The nine files are the claim's surface and nothing else: the schema file, its two tests, one semantic entry plus the regenerated registry, the two regenerated spec artefacts, the regenerated reference page, one changeset. **Right.**

One non-blocking reading: the refusal message hardcodes "`bar` / `column` / `horizontal-bar`" as the bar-family steer. That is the card's scope item 2 (steer to `table` or a bar-family type), not a restatement of the multi-measure set, which the same message prints from the constant.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/20958-dimensionless-multi-measure-refused.md`: `"@objectstack/spec": minor`, a `feat(spec)!:` summary, a BREAKING banner, an adr-0087 marker reading registered `dashboard-widget-dimensionless-multi-measure-refused`, and a `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` line followed by prose. **Matches what the diff publishes:** the surface gains two exports (the `minor` floor) and the accept set narrows (breaking-ness carried by the banner and the ADR-0087 disposition under the launch-window convention, where `check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major`). The shape is the metric-family precedent's changeset `17779-dashboard-metric-family-single-measure.md` line for line.
- The Clause-② parser (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`) reads the value as the first token after the key and the arm as the first word inside the parenthetical, so the trailing prose on the changeset's line does not unseat `narrowing`.
- **Clause-②:** `yes (narrowing)` on the PR body, on the changeset and on the card's claim; all three agree.
- `Check Changeset` concluded success on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (the os-dev-report lists four), each answered:

1. *Two exports, not one.* Answered right in ①.4; no escalation.
2. *No `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment despite the dispatch's hot-file note.* Answered right in ①.8: fragments accompany retirements with conversions, the precedent added none, and the step18 rationale merge test asks only that the fragments present stay sorted; no escalation.
3. *Metric family excluded though the card says "outside the multi-measure set".* Answered right in ①.2: the card's own pin forbids a second issue on the family; every type outside the set is still refused dimensionless by exactly one check; no escalation.
4. *`origin/main` moved after the merge lap and was not chased.* The PR reads mergeable at the time of this review; the seat re-reads the base and every check before landing. Not a contract matter; no action.

`open_questions`: none listed, none found.

Out-of-scope findings (two, carrier none): whether the seven types render several measures WITH a dimension is outside the card, and the entry states it as unanswered rather than implying it is covered — agreed, no escalation; the ablation tool refusing a replacement that is a substring of its anchor is a tooling observation — agreed, nothing owed here.
